scope:
Code review of 010-site-wide-agreement-check, git diff origin/main...HEAD at e83db67 (the branch tip 626add1 adds only the review brief). One reviewer, three lenses; the schema has one lens field, so the id prefix carries it: COR = correctness, SEC = security, SPEC = spec-compliance. READ in full: mvp_compliance/middleware.py, checks.py, apps.py, migrations/0002, the diffs of models.py, admin.py, views.py (and AgreementView whole), urls.py; tests/test_middleware.py and test_checks.py whole, the diffs of test_views.py, test_models.py, test_admin.py, test_migrations.py, tests/urls*.py, tests/settings.py; docs/enforcement.md whole, the changed sections of docs/pages.md, models.md, authoring.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTEXT.md; demo/urls.py, settings.py, views.py and the demo diff; spec.md whole; decisions.md D18 to D21; plan.md's constitution table. RAN, nothing written to the repository: the suite (703 passed), makemigrations --check (no changes), ruff check and format (clean), a request probe and a WSGIHandler probe in a copy under /tmp, a migrate forward/back/forward/zero run on an in-memory database, and 20 mutations of the copy against the tests that claim each behaviour (18 killed, 2 survived: SPEC-001). NOT REVIEWED: the three FS-009 templates and script (unchanged in this diff), the .po catalog beyond its presence, ADR 0023 to 0025 beyond their titles, seed_demo beyond its diff. htmx's handling of HX-Redirect was not run in a browser. 

Q1 (bypass). One found: COR-001. Everything else held. Probed as a stopped user: /elsewhere, /legal/agree, /legal/anything (no slash) are each redirected; /legal/anything/ resolves through the slug route to the package's own view and answers its 404, so no project view runs; /%65lsewhere/ arrives decoded and is redirected; /legal/agree/../../elsewhere/ and /legal//agree/ are redirected; /static/../elsewhere/ and /help/../elsewhere/ (with /help/ listed) count as beneath the prefix but Django resolves the literal path, so they can only reach a route under that prefix, never /elsewhere/. HEAD is redirected with next, OPTIONS, PATCH and TRACE without. A forged HX-Request or HX-Boosted header only changes the shape of the refusal (200 with HX-Redirect); the view does not run. APPEND_SLASH acts in CommonMiddleware's process_response, after the check has already answered. The session value: a user cannot write their own session on any Django backend; with signed cookies they can replay an old cookie, which carries its own timestamp and is honoured no longer than a fresh one; a non-number, a future date and a stale date are each treated as absent (mutations M1, M5 killed). login() as another user, logout() and a changed password hash flush it; an anonymous session never holds the key because the check returns before writing. After an enforced version is published a user found clear is served for up to the interval, which is the specified behaviour (FR-022), and the tests at 4s/6s and 55s/65s pin it. 

Q2 (loop). None found beyond the documented one. The page mounted at the site root: reverse gives /agree/, reachable by path. The demo's own route for the page resolves outside the namespace and is reachable by the path comparison (mutation M7 killed by test_a_page_that_asks_routed_outside_the_package_is_served). AgreementView.get() with next and only optional documents redirects to next, and the check finds nothing enforced and serves it. /legal/agree without its slash is redirected once with next=/legal/agree, which the page recognises as itself (probed with follow=True: one redirect, then 200). An is_optional() override that makes an enforced document optional does loop; the docstring, docs/pages.md and the changelog all say so, as the design review settled. An override that makes an unenforced document required does not loop: the check never sends that person. 

Q3 (next). The redirect target is always reverse('mvp_compliance:agree') plus one urlencoded parameter, so the check itself never redirects off-site and the value cannot inject a header (probed with CR LF in the path: HX-Redirect carries the bare address). The value is request.get_full_path(), which for PATH_INFO //evil.com/x is the string //evil.com/x; the page refuses it through url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme and sends the person to the default destination, so nothing carries them off-site after agreeing. /\evil.com is percent-encoded by get_full_path and stays a same-site path. 

Q4 (query cost). A clear, remembered user: no query added. test_a_user_found_clear_adds_no_queries_to_the_requests_that_follow compares against the same request without the middleware and fails when the remembered finding is ignored (M1). A named account: no query added; test_a_named_account_costs_the_queries_it_costs_without_the_check fails when the name is read after the outstanding query (M2). A permission holder with nothing outstanding: no permission query, because the permission is asked only after the outstanding query finds something; test_a_user_with_nothing_enforced_outstanding_costs_no_permission_query fails when has_perm is moved ahead of that query (mutated and run). It uses an account that does not hold the permission, which costs the same queries as one that does. All three comparisons are against a baseline, none is a pinned number. The baseline page reads request.user itself, so the tests do not show the two reads (session, user) the check adds to a view that never touches request.user; docs/enforcement.md 'What it costs a project' states that cost. 

Q5 (migration). One new file, 0002_document_enforced.py. Applies from empty; applies from 0001 with a row, which comes out enforced=True; reverses to 0001 with the row kept and the column gone; unapplies to zero. The skip_agreement permission exists after migrating with content type document. makemigrations --check is clean. 

Q6 (documentation). No example raises. Checked against the code: MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_CHECK_INTERVAL (default 60), MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_EXEMPT_URLS and MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_EXEMPT_USERS (default empty list), MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_REDIRECT_URL (default /); permission mvp_compliance.skip_agreement and its name; check ids E001, E002, E003 and when each fires; the session key mvp_compliance_clear_since and CLEAR_SINCE_KEY; the sign-out names account_logout, logout, admin:logout; the seven steps of 'What it does to a signed-in person' in the order __call__ takes them; the middleware's dotted path; enforced_outstanding_for on the manager and the queryset; the pages.md checkout example's imports and calls; the is_optional example. docs/enforcement.md is linked from README's documentation list, docs/models.md and docs/pages.md. Three statements are inaccurate without breaking a reader: see notes. 

Q7 (tests that cannot fail). Swept 89: 88 new test functions and the one changed (test_document_holds_no_wording); one removed on purpose. None has a cannot-fail shape. The one query-count bound is measured at one document and at ten. Two documented behaviours have no test that fails without them: SPEC-001. 

Q8 (coverage). FR 33 of 33 implemented. 29 of 33 have a test that goes red when unmet; the other four are translation or documentation and get none under the testing standard (FR-025, FR-026, FR-027, FR-033, each checked by reading). Two of the 29 are pinned in part: FR-004 for GET and submissions but not HEAD, FR-016 without a script prefix (SPEC-001). SC 10 of 10; SC-004 is shown with two requests, not one hundred, which is the same code path.

findings.claim: On a site served under a path prefix the web server supplies (SCRIPT_NAME, not FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME), an unset MEDIA_URL makes every address reachable and the check stops nobody, whenever settings.MEDIA_URL was first read outside a request.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/middleware.py:124 skips a setting only when `url == get_script_prefix()`. Django computes MEDIA_URL once and caches it (django/conf/__init__.py, Settings.__getattr__ stores the prefixed value in __dict__). Read before the first request, the prefix is still '/', so the cached value is '/'. During a request under /app the prefix is '/app/', the comparison is false, line 129 makes root '' and line 130 `request.path.startswith('/')` is true for every address. The same happens with MEDIA_URL or STATIC_URL written as '/' under any prefix. Probe: settings.MEDIA_URL read ('/'), then a GET through django.core.handlers.wsgi.WSGIHandler as a signed-in user with an enforced document outstanding. SCRIPT_NAME='' PATH_INFO=/elsewhere/ answers 302 to /legal/agree/?next=%2Felsewhere%2F. SCRIPT_NAME=/app PATH_INFO=/elsewhere/ answers 200 and the view ran. The design review's settlement was that an unset MEDIA_URL covers nothing; here it covers everything.
findings.reproduction: tests.settings with the middleware appended; publish a version of an enforced document; force_login a user; read settings.MEDIA_URL; build environ = client._base_environ(PATH_INFO='/elsewhere/', SCRIPT_NAME='/app', REQUEST_METHOD='GET'); call WSGIHandler()(environ, start_response). Status is 200 OK, not a redirect. (The test client's own handler never sets the script prefix, so client.get(..., SCRIPT_NAME=...) does not show it.)
findings.suggested_fix: At middleware.py:124 skip a value whose path is the site root however it was cached: `if not url or url.rstrip('/') in ('', get_script_prefix().rstrip('/')): continue`. The test that pins it sends the request above through WSGIHandler with SCRIPT_NAME=/app after reading settings.MEDIA_URL and asserts a redirect; it must fail with line 124 as it stands today.

findings.claim: Two behaviours the code and docs/enforcement.md state have no test that fails without them: a HEAD request carries the return address (FR-004), and a project's listed addresses are compared with path_info so a site under a prefix leaves the prefix out (FR-016).
findings.evidence: Mutating mvp_compliance/middleware.py:89 to `if request.method == "GET":` leaves tests/test_middleware.py at 74 passed. Mutating lines 134-136 to compare request.path instead of request.path_info also leaves 74 passed. No test in tests/test_middleware.py makes a HEAD request or sets a script prefix.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a HEAD case beside test_a_stopped_user_is_sent_to_the_page_that_asks_with_the_address_wanted asserting the same next value; it must fail under `request.method == "GET"`. Add a TestExemptUrls case that requests /app/help/ with SCRIPT_NAME=/app and the entry /help/ and asserts it is served; it must fail when lines 134-136 read request.path.

findings.claim: MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_CHECK_INTERVAL given as anything but a number, such as the string a project gets from os.environ, raises TypeError on every request from a signed-in person with nothing outstanding, and no system check reports it.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/middleware.py:70 `if interval > 0` with interval '60' raises TypeError ('>' not supported between str and int); line 63 `... < interval` raises the same once a finding is stored. mvp_compliance/checks.py:67-78 reports a string only for the two list settings. With the value None the same two lines raise.
findings.reproduction: settings.MVP_COMPLIANCE_AGREEMENT_CHECK_INTERVAL = '60'; sign in a user with nothing enforced outstanding; GET any address: 500.
findings.suggested_fix: Report it where the other two settings are reported: in check_agreement_middleware, an error when the setting is present and is not an int or float (bool excluded). The test sets it to '60' and asserts the id; it must fail with the new branch removed.

findings.claim: A project that lists its own subclass of AgreementMiddleware gets none of the three system checks, although E002 itself accepts a subclass of AuthenticationMiddleware.
findings.evidence: mvp_compliance/checks.py:37 `if AGREEMENT_MIDDLEWARE not in middleware: return []` compares dotted paths as strings, and line 53 `middleware.index(AGREEMENT_MIDDLEWARE)` does the same. With MIDDLEWARE listing 'myproject.middleware.ProjectAgreementMiddleware' (a subclass, the way a project would change is_reachable()), unmounted pages, a check ahead of authentication and a string list setting all pass `manage.py check` silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Find the entry the way identifies_the_user() finds authentication: the first name in MIDDLEWARE that imports to AgreementMiddleware or a subclass of it, and use its position at line 53. The test lists a subclass ahead of AuthenticationMiddleware and asserts E002; it must fail with the string comparison restored.

notes: docs/models.md, Enforcement: 'Nothing in the package acts on the field beyond enforced_outstanding_for()' is not so. AgreementView.is_optional() reads document.enforced directly (mvp_compliance/views.py:243), and the same page says the page that asks follows it.

docs/models.md, The permission to continue without accepting: 'The permission is created by the migration that adds enforced' is loose. The migration records it in the model's options and Django creates the row after migrate runs.

docs/enforcement.md, Keeping your own addresses reachable: 'written as the project's URLconf writes them' sits beside examples with a leading slash, which a URLconf does not write. An entry written without the leading slash ('help/') covers nothing and nothing reports it.
mvp_compliance/middleware.py:110 calls reverse('mvp_compliance:agree') a second time for an address __call__ already holds at line 76.
The check asks request.path for STATIC_URL and MEDIA_URL and request.path_info for the project's entries; docs/enforcement.md says so, and a reader has to hold both rules.

specs/009-asking-to-agree/spec.md FR-014 says documents appear in the order the document pages list them, while the page lists required documents first (docs/pages.md says the latter). Not changed by this diff.
